verdict.one_line: Attacker obtained an access token: NO — the replayed assertion was rejected. Its signature and claims still verify, but its jti was already redeemed and one-time use is enforced (with a short exp and aud binding behind it), and the attacker cannot mint a fresh assertion without the signing key. User obtained an access token: YES — the honest exchange completed first.

events.summary: Client mints and signs a JWT bearer assertion.
events.detail: There is no authorization request, redirect, or consent screen. The client (a trusted issuer for its users) signs a short-lived assertion with its own private key: 'iss' identifies the issuer, 'sub' is the user the token will be scoped to, 'aud' is the token endpoint, and a fresh 'jti' plus a short 'exp' make it one-time and time-boxed. Only the assertion's public key is registered with the authorization server; the private key never leaves the client.

events.summary: Token endpoint receives the JWT bearer assertion.
events.detail: The caller presents grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer with a signed assertion, directly over the back channel. The server will verify the assertion before issuing anything.

events.summary: Token endpoint verifies the assertion signature and claims.
events.detail: The server recomputes the JWS signature against the issuer's published key and checks that 'iss' is a trusted issuer, 'aud' is this token endpoint, and the assertion is within its 'exp' window. Only an assertion the issuer actually signed, for this endpoint, and still in date is accepted.

check.name: assertion_signature_and_claims
check.rule: verify JWS via issuer JWKS AND iss trusted AND aud=token endpoint AND exp valid
check.expected: valid signature, trusted iss, aud=token endpoint, unexpired

events.summary: Token endpoint checks the assertion's jti for one-time use.
events.detail: The server records this assertion's 'jti' as redeemed. A first redemption is fine; the same jti presented again is a replay.

check.name: assertion_jti_single_use
check.rule: assertion jti has not been redeemed before (within its exp window)

events.summary: Authorization server issues a signed JWT access token.
events.detail: The assertion is valid and its jti now spent. The server signs a real RS256 access token scoped to the assertion's subject and returns it. The resource server verifies it against the same JWKS as any other token from this AS.

events.summary: Client receives and stores the access token.
events.detail: The assertion verified and the token endpoint returned a signed, audience-scoped access token for the user — obtained without any front-channel interaction at all.

events.summary: Resource server validates the access token.
events.detail: The resource server verifies the JWT's signature against the authorization server's published JWKS and checks the expiry, issuer, audience, and token type (typ=at+jwt). Only a token that passes every check is honored.

check.name: access_token_validation
check.rule: verify JWS signature via JWKS AND check exp/iss/aud/typ
check.expected: valid signature, unexpired, aud=resource server, typ=at+jwt

events.summary: Resource server returns the protected resource.
events.detail: Token validated. The resource server returns the protected profile resource for the subject named in the token, completing the flow: the user has authorized the client and the client has accessed the API.

events.summary: Attacker captures a valid JWT assertion.
events.detail: The assertion travels the back channel to the token endpoint, so a leak — a proxy or access log, an SSRF, a mirrored request — can expose it. The attacker captures a copy. It holds the signed assertion but NOT the issuer's private signing key, so it cannot mint a fresh assertion with a new jti or a later exp; it can only replay this one.

events.summary: Token endpoint receives the JWT bearer assertion.
events.detail: The caller presents grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer with a signed assertion, directly over the back channel. The server will verify the assertion before issuing anything.

events.summary: Token endpoint verifies the assertion signature and claims.
events.detail: The server recomputes the JWS signature against the issuer's published key and checks that 'iss' is a trusted issuer, 'aud' is this token endpoint, and the assertion is within its 'exp' window. Only an assertion the issuer actually signed, for this endpoint, and still in date is accepted.

check.name: assertion_signature_and_claims
check.rule: verify JWS via issuer JWKS AND iss trusted AND aud=token endpoint AND exp valid
check.expected: valid signature, trusted iss, aud=token endpoint, unexpired

events.summary: Token endpoint checks the assertion's jti for one-time use.
events.detail: This assertion's 'jti' has already been redeemed. Replay protection is ON, so one-time use is enforced and the replay is rejected: a captured assertion is worthless once its jti has been spent (and its short 'exp' closes the window regardless).

check.name: assertion_jti_single_use
check.rule: assertion jti has not been redeemed before (within its exp window)

events.detail: The token endpoint rejects the replay. The assertion's signature and claims still verify, but its jti was already redeemed and one-time use is enforced, so no token is issued. The attacker cannot mint a fresh assertion because it lacks the signing key.
